# url

Types from the Go package `url` (a library PocketBase builds on), as JavaScript sees them: they turn up as values of [PocketBase's types](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase) and of hook events.

## url.URL

A URL represents a parsed URL (technically, a URI reference).

The general form represented is:

```
	[scheme:][//[userinfo@]host][/]path[?query][#fragment]
```

URLs that do not start with a slash after the scheme are interpreted as:

```
	scheme:opaque[?query][#fragment]
```

The Host field contains the host and port subcomponents of the URL.
When the port is present, it is separated from the host with a colon.
When the host is an IPv6 address, it must be enclosed in square brackets:
"[fe80::1]:80". The `net.joinHostPort` function combines a host and port
into a string suitable for the Host field, adding square brackets to
the host when necessary.

Note that the Path field is stored in decoded form: /%47%6f%2f becomes /Go/.
A consequence is that it is impossible to tell which slashes in the Path were
slashes in the raw URL and which were %2f. This distinction is rarely important,
but when it is, the code should use the [`URL.escapedPath`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) method, which preserves
the original encoding of Path. The Fragment field is also stored in decoded form,
use [`URL.escapedFragment`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) to retrieve the original encoding.

The [`URL.string`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) method uses the [`URL.escapedPath`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) method to obtain the path.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|

| `opaque` | <code>string // encoded opaque data</code> |  |
| `user?` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urluserinfo">Userinfo</a> // username and password information</code> |  |
| `host` | <code>string // &#34;host&#34; or &#34;host:port&#34; (see Hostname and Port methods)</code> |  |
| `path` | <code>string // path (relative paths may omit leading slash)</code> |  |
| `fragment` | <code>string // fragment for references (without &#39;#&#39;)</code> |  |
| `rawQuery` | <code>string</code> | RawQuery contains the encoded query values, without the initial '?'. Use URL.Query to decode the query. |
| `rawPath` | <code>string</code> | RawPath is an optional field containing an encoded path hint. See the EscapedPath method for more details. |
| `rawFragment` | <code>string</code> | RawFragment is an optional field containing an encoded fragment hint. See the EscapedFragment method for more details. |
| `forceQuery` | <code>boolean</code> | ForceQuery indicates whether the original URL contained a query ('?') character. When set, the String method will include a trailing '?', even when RawQuery is empty. |
| `omitHost` | <code>boolean</code> | OmitHost indicates the URL has an empty host (authority). When set, the String method will not include the host when it is empty. |
| `escapedPath()` | <code>(): string</code> | EscapedPath returns the escaped form of u.Path. In general there are multiple possible escaped forms of any path. EscapedPath returns u.RawPath when it is a valid escaping of u.Path. Otherwise EscapedPath ignores u.RawPath and computes an escaped form on its own. The [`URL.string`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) and [`URL.requestURI`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) methods use EscapedPath to construct their results. In general, code should call EscapedPath instead of reading u.RawPath directly. |
| `escapedFragment()` | <code>(): string</code> | EscapedFragment returns the escaped form of u.Fragment. In general there are multiple possible escaped forms of any fragment. EscapedFragment returns u.RawFragment when it is a valid escaping of u.Fragment. Otherwise EscapedFragment ignores u.RawFragment and computes an escaped form on its own. The [`URL.string`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) method uses EscapedFragment to construct its result. In general, code should call EscapedFragment instead of reading u.RawFragment directly. |
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> | String reassembles the [`URL`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) into a valid URL string. The general form of the result is one of: |
| `redacted()` | <code>(): string</code> | Redacted is like [`URL.string`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) but replaces any password with "xxxxx". Only the password in u.User is redacted. |
| `isAbs()` | <code>(): boolean</code> | IsAbs reports whether the [`URL`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) is absolute. Absolute means that it has a non-empty scheme. |
| `parse()` | <code>(ref: string): (<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl">URL</a>)</code> | Parse parses a [`URL`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) in the context of the receiver. The provided URL may be relative or absolute. Parse returns nil, err on parse failure, otherwise its return value is the same as [`URL.resolveReference`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl). |
| `resolveReference()` | <code>(ref: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl">URL</a>): (<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl">URL</a>)</code> | ResolveReference resolves a URI reference to an absolute URI from an absolute base URI u, per RFC 3986 Section 5.2. The URI reference may be relative or absolute. ResolveReference always returns a new [`URL`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl) instance, even if the returned URL is identical to either the base or reference. If ref is an absolute URL, then ResolveReference ignores base and returns a copy of ref. |

## url.Values

Values maps a string key to a list of values.
It is typically used for query parameters and form values.
Unlike in the http.Header map, the keys in a Values map
are case-sensitive.

Has everything <code>{ [key: string]: any }</code> has.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `get()` | <code>(key: string): string</code> | Get gets the first value associated with the given key. If there are no values associated with the key, Get returns the empty string. To access multiple values, use the map directly. |
| `set()` | <code>(key: string, value: string): void</code> | Set sets the key to value. It replaces any existing values. |
| `add()` | <code>(key: string, value: string): void</code> | Add adds the value to key. It appends to any existing values associated with key. |
| `del()` | <code>(key: string): void</code> | Del deletes the values associated with key. |
| `has()` | <code>(key: string): boolean</code> | Has checks whether a given key is set. |
| `clone()` | <code>(): <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlvalues">Values</a></code> | Clone creates a deep copy of the subject [`Values`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlvalues). |
| `encode()` | <code>(): string</code> | Encode encodes the values into “URL encoded” form ("bar=baz&foo=quux") sorted by key. |

## url.Userinfo

The Userinfo type is an immutable encapsulation of username and
password details for a [`URL`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/url#urlurl). An existing Userinfo value is guaranteed
to have a username set (potentially empty, as allowed by RFC 2396),
and optionally a password.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `username()` | <code>(): string</code> | Username returns the username. |
| `password()` | <code>(): [string, boolean]</code> | Password returns the password in case it is set, and whether it is set. |
| `string()` | <code>(): string</code> | String returns the encoded userinfo information in the standard form of "username[:password]". |
